newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Commission suspends meeting on Di Rupo.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Commission suspends meeting on Di Rupo.

text.p: A special Belgian parliamentary commission said on Wednesday it was suspending a meeting to assess fresh allegations of child sex against Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo.

Raymond Langendries, the president of parliament who also chairs the commission, told reporters: "The special commission has suspended its work." He said the commission would resume work on Wednesday afternoon as there would be a government statement and debate in the morning.

The meeting had started on Tuesday morning and heard a statement from the Prosecutor General of the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court and the only one which under Belgian law can investigate and try ministers and ex-ministers.
It also heard Di Rupo, a 45-year-old discreet homosexual and leading French-speaking socialist politician. He has always denied the allegations, described by some commission members as wafer thin.

During the meeting of the commission, made up of the main parties, differences emerged between the socialist coalition partners, who had sought to protect Di Rupo, and the liberal opposition, who are clamouring for his resignation.

Continuation of a High Court investigation would leave in doubt the future of Di Rupo, the number two in the centre-left coalition, and would paralyse the government of Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
